   135	\begin{proposition}
   136	[Affine chart is a Dedekind domain with fraction field \(K\)]
   137	  \label{thm:adelic_chartRing_isDedekindDomain}
   138	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.chartRing_isDedekindDomain}
   139	  \uses{def:isRegularInCodimensionOne}
   140	  % [scheidler] valuation rings / DVR foundations; [cff] Prop. 4.2 (DVR characterisation)
   141	  \source{scheidler-function-fields, cff-curves-function-fields}
   142	  Let \(U \subseteq C\) be a nonempty affine open with coordinate ring
   143	  \(A_U = \Gamma(U, \struct{C})\). Then \(A_U\) is a Dedekind domain and
   144	  the canonical map \(A_U \hookrightarrow K\) exhibits \(K\) as the field
   145	  of fractions of \(A_U\).
   146	\end{proposition}
   147	\begin{proof}
   148	  Since \(C\) is integral, \(A_U\) is an integral domain, and for a
   149	  nonempty affine open of an integral scheme the natural map to the
   150	  function field \(A_U \to K\) is injective with
   151	  \(\mathrm{IsFractionRing}\, A_U\, K\) (the localisation of \(A_U\) at
   152	  its generic point is \(K\)); this is the affine-chart fraction-field
   153	  statement used to build \(\texttt{functionFieldIso}\)
   154	  (\Cref{def:functionFieldIso}). It remains to verify the Dedekind
   155	  axioms. \(A_U\) is Noetherian: \(C\) is of finite type over the field
   156	  \(k\), hence locally Noetherian, so \(A_U\) is a finitely generated
   157	  \(k\)-algebra and Noetherian. \(A_U\) is a domain that is not a field
   158	  (a curve has closed points), of Krull dimension one: every nonzero
   159	  prime of \(A_U\) is maximal because the corresponding point of \(U\)
   160	  has codimension one in the one-dimensional \(C\). At each such
   161	  height-one prime \(\mathfrak p\), the localisation
   162	  \((A_U)_{\mathfrak p} = \struct{C, x}\) is the stalk at the
   163	  corresponding codimension-one point \(x\), which is a discrete
   164	  valuation ring by \(\mathrm{IsRegularInCodimensionOne}\)
   165	  (\Cref{def:isRegularInCodimensionOne}), automatic here from the
   166	  smoothness of \(C\). A one-dimensional Noetherian domain whose
   167	  localisations at height-one primes are discrete valuation rings is
   168	  integrally closed, hence Dedekind by the standard characterisation
   169	  (a Noetherian integrally closed domain of dimension \(\le 1\)).
   170	  \paragraph{Gate.} The one non-formal input is ``smooth curve chart
   171	  \(\Rightarrow\) regular chart'', supplied here by
   172	  \(\mathrm{IsRegularInCodimensionOne}\). Should the passage from
   173	  smoothness of \(C.\hom\) to that class be unavailable at a use site, it
   174	  is threaded as the single-field class
   175	  \(\mathrm{HasDedekindChart}\, C\), discharged by \(\texttt{inferInstance}\)
   176	  once the regularity instance is present.
   177	\end{proof}

   181	[Point valuation and residue degree]
   182	  \label{def:adelic_pointValuation}
   183	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.pointValuation}
   184	  \uses{thm:adelic_chartRing_isDedekindDomain, def:order_at_point, lem:order_eq_order_restrict}
   185	  % [scheidler] p. 24 (deg P = [F_P : K]); [cff] (C2) deg P = dim_K O_P/P
   186	  \source{scheidler-function-fields, cff-curves-function-fields}
   187	  Let \(P\) be a prime divisor whose point lies in a nonempty affine open
   188	  \(U\), with Dedekind chart \(A_U\)
   189	  (\Cref{thm:adelic_chartRing_isDedekindDomain}). The prime \(P\)
   190	  determines a height-one prime \(\mathfrak p_P\) of \(A_U\), and the
   191	  discrete valuation of the challenge,
   192	  \(v_P = \mathrm{order}\, P\) on \(K\) (\Cref{def:order_at_point}),
   193	  coincides with the \(\mathfrak p_P\)-adic valuation of \(A_U\) on
   194	  \(K = \operatorname{Frac} A_U\). Its residue field is
   195	  \(\kappa(P) = A_U/\mathfrak p_P = \struct{C, P}/\mathfrak m_P\), and the
   196	  \emph{degree} of \(P\) is the finite number
   197	  \(\deg P = \dim_k \kappa(P) = [\kappa(P) : k]\).
   198	\end{definition}
   199	\begin{proof}
   200	  The stalk \(\struct{C, P}\) is the localisation \((A_U)_{\mathfrak p_P}\)
   201	  because \(P\) lies in the affine \(U\); its normalised valuation, whose
   202	  \(\mathrm{WithZero.log}\) is \(\mathrm{order}\, P\)
   203	  (\Cref{def:order_at_point}), is by definition the
   204	  \(\mathfrak p_P\)-adic valuation. Independence of the chosen chart is
   205	  the naturality \Cref{lem:order_eq_order_restrict}: \(\mathrm{order}\)
   206	  is invariant under open-immersion restriction, so any two affine charts
   207	  containing \(P\) give the same valuation on \(K\). Finiteness of
   208	  \(\deg P\): \(\kappa(P)\) is the residue field of a closed point of the
   209	  finite-type \(k\)-scheme \(C\); choosing a nonconstant \(x \in K\)
   210	  bounds \([\kappa(P) : k] \le [K : k(x)] < \infty\).
   211	\end{proof}

   214	  \label{def:adelic_divisor_degree}
   215	  \source{scheidler-function-fields, cff-curves-function-fields}
   216	  \uses{def:adelic_pointValuation, def:codim1_cycles}
   217	
   218	  For a Weil divisor \(D=\sum_P n_P[P]\) on a curve over \(k\), define its
   219	  residue-weighted degree by

   221	    \deg_k(D)=\sum_P n_P[\kappa(P):k].

section Sections

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]

/-- **N3 — the Riemann–Roch section subgroup `Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D))`.** For an open
`U ⊆ X` and a Weil divisor `D`, the set of rational functions `f ∈ K(X)` whose
order along every prime divisor `P` meeting `U` is at least `-D(P)`:
`Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D)) = { f : f = 0 ∨ ∀ P ∈ U, ord_P f ≥ -D(P) }`.

The `f = 0` disjunct encodes the convention `ord_P 0 = +∞` (the project's junk
convention gives `ord_P 0 = 0`, so the zero function must be admitted separately).
Closure under addition is the `order` ultrametric `order_add_ge_min`. -/
def sectionOfDivisor (U : X.Opens) (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
    AddSubgroup X.functionField where
  carrier := { f | f = 0 ∨ ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
    -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f }
  zero_mem' := Or.inl rfl
  add_mem' := by
    intro f g hf hg
    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hfne
    · simpa using hg
    rcases eq_or_ne g 0 with rfl | hgne
    · simpa using hf
    rcases eq_or_ne (f + g) 0 with h0 | h0
    · exact Or.inl h0
    refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
    have hcf := (hf.resolve_left hfne) P hP
    have hcg := (hg.resolve_left hgne) P hP
    calc -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)
        ≤ min (Scheme.RationalMap.order P f) (Scheme.RationalMap.order P g) :=
          le_min hcf hcg
      _ ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P (f + g) := order_add_ge_min P hfne hgne h0
  neg_mem' := by
    intro f hf
    rcases hf with rfl | hf
    · exact Or.inl (by simp)
    · refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
      rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_neg]
      exact hf P hP

/-- Membership in `Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D))`. -/
theorem mem_sectionOfDivisor {U : X.Opens} {D : X.WeilDivisor}
    {f : X.functionField} :
    f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D ↔ f = 0 ∨ ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
      -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- Membership for a nonzero function: only the order condition remains. -/
theorem mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero {U : X.Opens} {D : X.WeilDivisor}
    {f : X.functionField} (hf : f ≠ 0) :
    f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D ↔ ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
      -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f := by
  rw [mem_sectionOfDivisor, or_iff_right hf]

    81	\paragraph{Residue-degree bookkeeping.}
    82	Because \(k\) need not be algebraically closed, every place carries a
    83	\emph{residue degree}. For a prime divisor \(P\) with residue field
    84	\(\kappa(P) = \struct{C, P}/\mathfrak{m}_P\), set
    85	\[
    86	  \deg P \;=\; [\kappa(P) : k] \;=\; \dim_k \kappa(P) \;<\; \infty,
    87	  \qquad
    88	  \deg_k D \;=\; \sum_P D(P)\,\deg P .
    89	\]
    90	Over an algebraically closed \(k\) one has \(\deg P = 1\) and this
    91	weighted degree specializes to the coefficient degree of
    92	\Cref{def:divisor_degree} and \cref{thm:divisor_degree_hom}.  Over a general
    93	field the weighted degree used here is different from the coefficient sum;
    94	the whole \(\chi\)-ledger below carries the residue degrees.  It is recorded
    95	formally in \Cref{def:adelic_divisor_degree} after the point valuation has been
    96	constructed.  In this chapter, an unadorned \(\deg D\) means this
    97	residue-weighted degree \(\deg_k D\).
    98

   100	\(i(D) = \dim_k \check{H}^1(D)\), and
   101	\(\chi(D) = \ell(D) - i(D)\) for the Euler characteristic. The genus is
   102	\(g = i(0) = \dim_k \check{H}^1(0)\) (\Cref{def:genus}, once
   103	\Cref{thm:adelic_module_finite_genus} makes it a finite number).

author: sync
chapter: 'Adelic Riemann--Roch: the repartition cokernel (RR.A)'
content_type: definition
created: '2026-07-26T02:41:20'

label: def:adelic_divisor_degree
lean_status: empty
order: 1831
title: Residue-weighted degree
type: tex
updated: '2026-07-26T02:44:57'
---
For a Weil divisor \(D=\sum_P n_P[P]\) on a curve over \(k\), define its
  residue-weighted degree by
  \[
    \deg_k(D)=\sum_P n_P[\kappa(P):k].
  \]
  The sum is finite because a Weil divisor has finite support.  If \(k\) is
  algebraically closed, every closed point has residue field \(k\), so
  \(\deg_k\) agrees with the coefficient degree of
  \Cref{def:divisor_degree}.---
author: sync
chapter: 'Adelic Riemann--Roch: the repartition cokernel (RR.A)'
content_type: definition
created: '2026-07-26T02:44:57'
generated: blueprint
label: def:adelic_residue_degree
lean_status: empty
order: 1830
title: Residue field and residue degree
type: tex
updated: '2026-07-26T02:44:57'
---
If \(P\) lies in a nonempty affine open \(U\), it determines a height-one
  prime \(\mathfrak p_P\) of the Dedekind chart
  \(A_U=\Gamma(U,\struct C)\).  Its residue field and residue degree are
  \[
    \kappa(P)=A_U/\mathfrak p_P
      =\struct{C,P}/\mathfrak m_P,
    \qquad
    \deg P=[\kappa(P):k]=\dim_k\kappa(P).
  \]
  The stalk \(\struct{C, P}\) is the localisation \((A_U)_{\mathfrak p_P}\)
  because \(P\) lies in \(U\).  The definition is independent of the chart,
  and \(\deg P\) is finite by Zariski's lemma because \(P\) is a closed point
  of the finite-type \(k\)-scheme \(C\).---
